article_title: How data centres became the sleeper issue that could decide the US midterms

tasks.prompt: What is the central argument of the article?
options: Data-centre expansion has rapidly become a cross-party local backlash that could influence US midterm races.
Federal senators directly approve every data-centre permit.
Most American voters consider AI infrastructure unimportant.
Data centres have already been banned in every US state.
tasks.correct_answer: Data-centre expansion has rapidly become a cross-party local backlash that could influence US midterm races.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה טוענת שהתנגדות מקומית למרכזי נתונים הפכה במהירות לסוגיה חוצת מפלגות שעשויה להשפיע על בחירות האמצע.

tasks.prompt: What scale of growth does the Pew report suggest for US data centres?
options: Their number will fall below 1,000.
Only one new centre is planned.
The current total of about 3,000 could double within a few years.
Every centre will expand to six square miles.
tasks.correct_answer: The current total of about 3,000 could double within a few years.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לפי הדוח המצוטט, בארה״ב פועלים כ־3,000 מרכזי נתונים ומספרם עשוי להכפיל את עצמו בתוך כמה שנים.

tasks.prompt: What does “180-degree turn” mean in the description of the senator?
options: A complete change in position or attention
A delay of exactly six months
A return trip between two states
A technical change inside a computer
tasks.correct_answer: A complete change in position or attention
tasks.explanation_hebrew: 180-degree turn הוא שינוי מוחלט: הסנאטור עבר מחוסר עניין לעיסוק קבוע בהשפעות מרכזי הנתונים ובחקיקה.

tasks.prompt: Which concerns did residents in several states raise about data centres?
options: Only the colour of the buildings
A lack of mobile-phone shops
Foreign ownership of every project
Noise, size, construction, resource use and rapid local approvals
tasks.correct_answer: Noise, size, construction, resource use and rapid local approvals
tasks.explanation_hebrew: התושבים העלו חששות מגודל ובנייה, רעש תפעולי, השפעה על אוויר, מים ואנרגיה ומהירות האישורים.

tasks.prompt: Why can data centres create political conflict even within the Republican Party?
options: Local conservative voters may oppose projects that national pro-AI leaders strongly support.
Republican states do not use the internet.
Only Democrats live near data centres.
Federal law requires Republicans to reject every local permit.
tasks.correct_answer: Local conservative voters may oppose projects that national pro-AI leaders strongly support.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההתנגדות קיימת גם בקרב שמרנים, ולכן פוליטיקאים מקומיים עלולים להתנגש עם הנהגה לאומית התומכת בצמיחת AI ללא הגבלה.

tasks.prompt: Why does the article call data centres a “sleeper issue”?
options: They operate only at night.
They are built inside hotels.
They seemed secondary at first but have become unexpectedly important to the election.
Voters are unaware that computers use electricity.
tasks.correct_answer: They seemed secondary at first but have become unexpectedly important to the election.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: sleeper issue היא סוגיה שנראתה שולית או שקטה, אך צברה כוח ועלולה להשפיע באופן משמעותי על הבחירות.

tasks.prompt: How have politicians in Arizona, Ohio and Texas responded to public pressure over data centres?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין את עצירת הטבות המס באריזונה, ריכוך התמיכה של הסטד באוהיו, והנסיגה של אבוט בטקסס מתמיכה נלהבת להבעת חששות.
expected_points: Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs enacted a three-year pause on new data-centre tax breaks.
Ohio Senator John Husted softened his support and said local citizens and officials should decide.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott shifted from boasting about AI leadership to citing safety and quality-of-life concerns.
Candidates in these states have made regulation, pauses or opposition part of election campaigns.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the economic and political debate over new data centres.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג טענות לגבי השקעה ומשרות מול ממצאים על מספר משרות מוגבל, חששות סביבתיים וקהילתיים, הטבות מס, והתמריצים של פוליטיקאים להגיב לבוחרים.
expected_points: Supporters say data centres bring investment and better-paying local jobs.
Research cited in the article estimates only 100–200 local jobs per centre and little effect on wages.
Residents worry about noise, construction, land, air, water, energy and the approval process.
Politicians are responding with proposed regulation, tax-break pauses or campaign opposition because voter anger crosses party lines.

tasks.prompt: Why might temporary moratoriums fail to resolve the underlying data-centre conflict?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר שההקפאות מוגבלות בזמן, אינן קובעות פתרון קבוע למשאבים ולאישורים, והאקלים הפוליטי עלול להשתנות לפני פקיעתן.
expected_points: Many proposed pauses last only one to three years.
They delay construction without necessarily creating permanent rules for water, energy, pollution or local consent.
Public attention and political incentives may shift before the pauses expire.
Companies could resume rapid development if no durable policy replaces the moratorium.

tasks.prompt: Write a concise policy framework for deciding whether a local data-centre project should be approved.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציע הליך שקוף הכולל שיתוף ציבור, בדיקת צריכת משאבים וזיהום, הערכת תעסוקה והטבות מס, דרישות הפחתה ובקרה מתמשכת.
expected_points: Require transparent disclosure of land, water, energy, emissions, noise and backup-generator use.
Give local residents meaningful participation before permits or tax incentives are approved.
Compare credible job and wage benefits with infrastructure costs and public subsidies.
Set enforceable mitigation, monitoring and review conditions, with clear consequences for non-compliance.
